old: Replacing a and b by a − b lowers the total by 2b, an even number, so the total always stays odd or always stays even. 1 + 2 + … + 10 = 55 is odd, so the last number is odd. It is also never more than 10, the largest number on the board, so 55 is impossible: only 7 is left. 7 can really be reached: 2 − 1, 5 − 4, 7 − 6 and 9 − 8 give four 1s; 1 − 1 twice gives two 0s, and 0 − 0 = 0; then 10 − 3 = 7 and 7 − 0 = 7.
new: Replacing a and b by a − b lowers the total by 2b, an even number, so the total always stays odd or always stays even. The starting total 1 + 2 + … + 10 = 55 is odd, so the last number is odd. It is also never more than 10, the largest number on the board, so 55 is impossible: only 7 is left. The number 7 can really be reached: 2 − 1, 5 − 4, 7 − 6 and 9 − 8 give four 1s; 1 − 1 twice gives two 0s, and 0 − 0 = 0; then 10 − 3 = 7 and 7 − 0 = 7.
